places.name: Old Bus Depot Markets
places.why: Every Sunday by the lake: food stalls and handmade goods in the old bus depot.

places.name: Questacon
places.why: The science centre: hands-on exhibits that are more fun with friends than you'd admit.

places.name: National Gallery of Australia
places.why: The national art collection, plus the sculpture garden outside.

places.name: National Museum of Australia
places.why: On Acton Peninsula right next to ANU, an easy afternoon.

places.name: Australian War Memorial
places.why: The memorial and its galleries, at the end of Anzac Parade.

places.name: Canberra Glassworks
places.why: Glass art studios and a gallery in the old Kingston Powerhouse.

places.name: Mount Ainslie
places.why: Take the paved Kokoda summit trail from behind the War Memorial for the view over the city.

places.name: Lake Burley Griffin
places.why: Walk or ride the paths around the lake in the middle of the city.

places.name: National Arboretum
places.why: Forests from around the world, big skies and room for a picnic.

places.name: Australian National Botanic Gardens
places.why: Native plant gardens on Black Mountain, a walk from campus.

places.name: Haig Park
places.why: A long, tree-lined park through Braddon and Turner, a few minutes from Lonsdale Street.

places.name: Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve
places.why: A day trip out of the city: wildlife, wetlands and bush walks.

places.name: L'épi Artisan Bakery
places.why: French-style bakery with many sourdoughs, a signature pain d'épi baguette, boysenberry danishes and cakes.

places.name: Café June
places.why: Braddon brunch café (the refreshed Elemental) with a blueberry bagel, chilli scrambled hash and iced Biscoff latte.

places.name: Brod Burger
places.why: Flame-grilled burgers and Brod dogs at South.Point, plus a bar pouring local wine, spirits and beer.

places.name: Tak Kee Roast Inn
places.why: Dickson's long-running Cantonese BBQ: roast meats with rice, wonton soup and laksa, in generous affordable serves.

places.name: Hing Win Wonton and Claypot Rice
places.why: Cantonese comfort food in Marketplace Gungahlin: house-made prawn wontons, crispy claypot rice and sizzling steaks.

places.name: 101c Hotpot
places.why: All-you-can-eat Sichuan and Chongqing hotpot for $49 a head in Dickson, a spicy, messy meal with friends.

places.name: CBD Dumpling House
places.why: Casual dumpling house with 20+ fillings and long tables, a good bet for a big group on a budget.

places.name: Ginseng
places.why: Trolley-service Cantonese yum cha with handmade dumplings, Sat to Mon sittings; go with a group to try more.

places.name: Gelato Messina
places.why: Messina's first Canberra gelato shop, in Braddon, with creative flavours like Milo and milk jam 'Breakfast in Canberra'.

places.name: Asteri
places.why: Greek taverna in Mawson with grilled octopus, moussaka and mezze, a sunny outdoor area and themed event nights.

places.name: Bombay Duck
places.why: Indian in No Name Lane serving spicy skewers and comforting curries seven days a week.

places.name: Kita
places.why: All-night Indonesian diner with mie goreng, soto ayam and Oreo-topped drinks; no bookings, 60-minute table slots.

places.name: Gianni's
places.why: Neighbourhood Italian in Belconnen from the Briscola founder, bigger and brighter, with the signature tiramisu.

places.name: Ikigai Ramen
places.why: Neon-lit Gungahlin ramen joint serving tonkotsu broth until midnight.

places.name: Ramen O
places.why: Popular Belconnen ramen spot tucked into a plain building, serving authentic ramen and gyoza.

places.name: Sikdang
places.why: Korean in Bailey's Corner with kimchi pancake, tteokbokki, bibimbap and soft tofu stew, plus soju and Korean beer.

places.name: Al Manoosh Lebanese Bakery
places.why: Small family-run Lebanese bakery in Mawson for breakfast and lunch: shakshuka, musabaha, zaatar and labne.

places.name: Jarochos
places.why: Family-run Mexican from a Veracruz owner: suadero and birria tacos, three house salsas, weekend brunch.

places.name: Canberra Momo House
places.why: Nepalese in Gungahlin Place known for momo dumplings, flavour-packed curries and rice-and-dhido sets.

places.name: Snapper & Co
places.why: Lakeside fish and chips and burgers at Yarralumla, with a deck, courtyard and lawns that welcome families.

places.name: Kinn Thai
places.why: Thai restaurant on level 1 at Westfield Woden, a sibling of the city Kinn, serving authentic Thai dishes.

places.name: Au Lac
places.why: Fully vegan Vietnamese-style restaurant on Woolley Street, with a menu of fresh, flavourful plant-based dishes.

places.name: O Bach
places.why: Vietnamese in Greenway praised for a crackling-pork banh mi, plus pho and laksa.

places.name: The Whale Tea
places.why: City Walk bubble tea shop with fruity green teas, tea slushies, yogurt or cloud drinks and cake-flavoured icy teas.

places.name: The Cupping Room
places.why: ONA's University Avenue café nicknamed 'The Cuppo': sunny windows, reserve coffees and brunch like chorizo benedict.

places.name: Caphs
places.why: Manuka's long-running café, open all day and night, known for schnitzel, breakfast burritos and pasta.

places.name: Trust Cafe
places.why: Alcohol-free, volunteer-run evening café above King O'Malley's, with DJs and events, open 4pm to midnight on weekdays.

places.name: ONA Coffee House
places.why: Specialty roaster's Fyshwick café with a heated deck, classic café food and a welcome for remote workers.

places.name: Adore Tea
places.why: Teahouse and tea boutique serving tea-infused quiche, scones and wraps plus iced teas, with a kids' menu.

places.name: Cypher Brewing Co
places.why: Gungahlin brewery with 14 house beers, pub food, live music and a playground for the kids.

places.name: Devil You Don't
places.why: Basement cocktail bar in NewActon with velvet booths, classics plus inventive drinks, open to midnight Thursday to Saturday.

places.name: BentSpoke Brewing Co
places.why: Braddon craft brewery with 18 house beers on tap, pub food and a casual, lively crowd.

places.name: Edgar's Inn
places.why: Ainslie pub with a beer garden, upstairs grill, wine bar and pizzeria, set up for casual group drinks and meals.

places.name: Bar Rochford
places.why: Cosy first-floor wine bar in the Melbourne Building with local wines, port and sherry, and photo-worthy small plates.

places.name: Four Winds Vineyard
places.why: Murrumbateman cellar door with wine flights, wood-fired pizzas and build-your-own deli platters, called family-friendly.

places.name: Kingpin
places.why: Tenpin bowling with bars, karaoke and escape rooms all in one spot inside the Canberra Centre.

places.name: Riddle Room
places.why: Indoor escape rooms, several themed, with a 60-minute timer and group deals for 2 to 18+ players.

places.name: PowerKart Raceway
places.why: Indoor go-karting with glow-in-the-dark mini golf, VR and arcade games, five minutes from Parliament House.

places.name: Phillip Swimming and Ice Skating Centre

places.name: BlocHaus Bouldering
places.why: Indoor bouldering gym with 850 sqm of short walls and padded mats, so no ropes or partner needed.

places.name: Hey Show Karaoke
places.why: Private karaoke with 12 themed rooms, some big enough for 30 people, plus food and drinks.

places.name: First Strike Laser Tag
places.why: Outdoor forest laser tag with capture-point and sniper games, one-hour sessions for up to 12 players.

places.name: Holey Moley
places.why: Indoor themed 18-hole mini golf with a bar, quick-play rooms, karaoke and ball pits, built for friends and dates.

places.name: Cockington Green Gardens

places.name: Canberra Potters
places.why: Community ceramics centre where beginners can try the wheel for $10 or handbuilding for $5 at its Fired Up open day.

places.name: BOUNCE Belconnen
places.why: Indoor trampoline park with free-jump areas, dodgeball, a ninja course, wall climb and a cliff jump.

places.name: National Zoo & Aquarium

places.name: Stromlo Forest Park

places.name: Kambah Pool

places.name: Palace Electric Cinema
places.why: NewActon arthouse cinema with eight screens, a Prosecco bar and recliner seats, plus festivals and special screenings.

places.name: The Street Theatre
places.why: A small City West live performance venue that stages music nights, theatre and new local work.

places.name: Smith's Alternative
places.why: Bookshop, café and small stage in one: jazz, folk and experimental sets, open mics and poetry nights.

places.name: National Portrait Gallery
places.why: A free gallery of portraits of notable Australians beside the High Court and National Gallery, with a cafe on site.

places.name: Canberra Theatre Centre
places.why: Canberra's main performing arts centre, with a 2026 mix of musicals, dance, Bell Shakespeare, comedy and family shows.

places.name: Capital Region Farmers Market

places.name: Raku

places.name: Mama Dough

places.name: Dickson Dumpling House

places.name: Timezone Woden

places.name: Pitch Black

places.name: Lake Tuggeranong

places.name: eightysix

places.name: Grease Monkey

places.name: Italian and Sons

places.name: Lazy Su

places.name: Akiba

places.name: Inka

places.name: Raku Japanese Bar & Restaurant

places.name: Rebel Rebel

places.name: Azuma Den

places.name: Molto Italian

places.name: Akaluck Restaurant

places.name: Chatkazz

places.name: Ginger & Spice Asian Cuisine

places.name: Moo Moo

places.name: Ogawa

places.name: Mirchi

places.name: TAIWA SUSHI

places.name: Banh Mi Ko

places.name: 54 Benjamin

places.name: Moo Moo Frozen Yoghurt (Braddon)

places.name: Black and White Espresso

places.name: High Road

places.name: Hungry Beagle

places.name: Kambah Inn

places.name: Johnny Gio's

places.why: Indoors: weekly bookable dance classes in Open, Mover and Advanced levels; the Open class needs no dance experience.

places.name: Funland Canberra
places.why: Indoors: giant jungle gym, soft play and interactive toys for children of all ages, with a cafe for parents; no booking needed.

places.name: Let's Play Indoor Playground & Cafe
places.why: Indoors: slides and climbing structures plus a baby and toddler zone, with a healthy cafe on site.

places.name: Little Amigos
places.why: Indoors: play zones with slides, train rides and a ball pool for little kids, inside the Canberra Outlet.

places.name: Sprouts Corner Indoor Playcentre
places.why: Indoors: a nature-inspired play centre and cafe for children aged 0 to 7 and their families.

places.name: Inflatable World Kambah
places.why: Indoors: a completely inflatable playground where kids can bounce and climb out of the sun.

places.name: Lollipop's Playland & Cafe
places.why: Indoors: a play centre with a dedicated toddler area and plenty for older kids, with a cafe for parents.

places.name: Flip Out Majura
places.why: Indoors: a 2,000 square metre trampoline park with foam pits, a parkour area, arcade games and party rooms.

places.name: Yarralumla Play Station
places.why: Four acres of hedge mazes and the Infinity Room, mini golf of Canberra icons, farm animals and a miniature railway by the lake.

places.name: Canberra Reptile Zoo
places.why: Meet reptiles, frogs and native animals up close, with keepers on hand and some animals you can touch.

places.name: Canberra International Golf Centre
places.why: Two-storey driving range open till late, plus an 18-hole pitch and putt and a mini golf course.

places.name: Floating Sauna Lake Burley Griffin
places.why: Wood-fired saunas on a floating pontoon with lake views, with a dip in the lake or a cold shower on deck between rounds.

places.name: Jindii EcoSpa
places.why: Day spa treatments built around native botanical ingredients, in a garden setting inside the Botanic Gardens.

places.name: Yoga Paws Puppy Yoga
places.why: Weekend 60-minute beginner-friendly yoga with puppies roaming nearby; sessions alternate between Phillip and Narrabundah, ages 12 and over.

places.name: Beltana Farm Truffle Hunts
places.why: Follow truffle dogs through the oak plantation and pull a truffle from the ground, then a long lunch or a hands-on cooking class; truffle season only.

places.name: Wine Hopper Murrumbateman
places.why: Hop-on, hop-off chauffeured day tour of the Murrumbateman cellar doors, so nobody has to drive.

places.name: Balloon Aloft
places.why: Sunrise hot air balloon rides over Canberra, daily and weather dependent, from the city's original balloon operator.

places.name: Paranormal Investigations at Old Parliament House
places.why: After-dark ghost hunt through the heritage rooms and corridors of Old Parliament House, using ghost-hunting tools and spirit communication.

places.name: Wine Tasting and Stargazing at Mount Majura
places.why: An hour tasting six wines with cheese and charcuterie, then an hour of guided stargazing with an astronomer, minutes from the city.

places.name: Love Boats Canberra
places.why: Walk-up hire of licence-free electric boats or pedal boats on Lake Burley Griffin, from three lakeside locations.

places.name: GoBoat Canberra
places.why: Self-drive electric picnic boat for up to eight with a table on board; no boat licence needed and dogs are welcome.

places.name: The Paddle Hub
places.why: Stand-up paddle board and kayak hire on Yarralumla Bay run by the YMCA; seasonal October to April and by group booking.

places.name: Canberra Miniature Railway
places.why: Ride miniature steam, electric and petrol trains around about 1.5 km of track on public running days held twice a month.

places.name: Treetops Adventure Canberra
places.why: Outdoor treetop courses in Majura Pines with 90 obstacles and 16 ziplines, two to twenty metres up, for ages three and up.

places.name: Delta Force Paintball
places.why: Outdoor paintball on movie-set style fields, with MiniBall for kids from ten and standard paintball from sixteen.

places.name: Forest Park Riding and Equitation School
places.why: One-hour trail rides for beginners to advanced riders aged seven and up, with lessons and school-holiday programs, 20 minutes from the city.

places.name: Canberra Walk-in Aviary
places.why: Walk through a planted aviary of nearly 600 birds and feed the free-flying parrots; entry includes a plate of bird food.

places.name: VR Canberra
places.why: Indoors: virtual reality games and VR escape rooms for groups, in Mitchell.

places.name: Zone Bowling Belconnen
places.why: Indoors: ten-pin bowling with a Timezone arcade next door, a good wet-weather group outing in Belconnen.

places.name: Dickson Pool
places.why: Outdoor summer pool with a 50 m pool, heated learners pool, toddler pool and splash park; reopened for the season on 31 October 2026.

places.name: Manuka Pool
places.why: Seasonal outdoor public pool in Manuka, reopened for the warmer months on 24 October 2026.

places.name: Canberra Olympic Pool
places.why: Outdoor Olympic pool in the city centre with toddler and dive pools in summer, reopened for the season on 1 November 2026.

places.name: Gungahlin Leisure Centre
places.why: Indoors: public swimming pool and leisure centre in Gungahlin, open all year round with group fitness and swim lessons.

places.name: Lakeside Leisure Centre
places.why: Indoors: public pool and leisure centre in Tuggeranong, open all year round.

places.name: Erindale Leisure Centre
places.why: Indoors: public pool and leisure centre in the Erindale Centre, open all year round with group fitness classes.

places.name: Stromlo Leisure Centre
places.why: Indoors: public pool and leisure centre at Stromlo Forest Park, open all year round.

places.name: Queanbeyan Aquatic Centre
places.why: A 25 m indoor pool all year, plus a 50 m outdoor pool and wet play area from October to March.

places.name: Clonakilla
places.why: Taste shiraz viognier at the cellar door of the region's first modern vineyard, by the fire in winter or on the vineyard-view patio in summer.

places.name: Helm Wines
places.why: Riesling tastings in an 1888 National Trust schoolhouse, run by the family that has made wine here since 1973.

places.name: Shaw Estate
places.why: Seated four or six wine tastings in a modern cellar door, with a Mediterranean restaurant on site; a long lunch for a group.

places.name: Collector Wines
places.why: Guided cool-climate tastings in the restored Hazeldean building in Collector village, about 40 minutes from Canberra.

places.name: Tallagandra Hill
places.why: Winery with a concert programme: live gigs among the vines, plus cellar door tastings for groups booked in advance.

places.name: McKellar Ridge Wines
places.why: Small family cellar door where the owners pour cool-climate wines themselves on weekends.

places.name: Yarrh Wines
places.why: Rammed-earth cellar door with western views and low-intervention wines; tastings, charcuterie or a two-course lunch.

places.name: The Vintner's Daughter
places.why: Guided tastings in the cellar door or on the verandah; early arrivals can join morning feeding time with the farm animals.

places.name: Pankhurst Wines
places.why: Estate-grown wines with some of the region's best views, poured by the owners about 20 minutes from Canberra.

places.name: Heywood Cellar Door and Restaurant (Nick O'Leary)
places.why: Guided tastings at the bar, then a farm-to-table restaurant meal paired with Nick O'Leary wines, with Brindabella views.

places.name: Lerida Estate
places.why: Pinot noir and shiraz with views over Lake George, with Cafe Lerida and cheese boards on site.

places.name: Mount Majura Vineyard
places.why: Guided tastings in a cellar door overlooking the vines, only 15 minutes from the city; a winter truffle tasting runs with The Truffle Farm.

places.name: Poachers Pantry Smokehouse and Vineyard
places.why: Splash tastings, a smokehouse restaurant and a farm shop with coffee, all on a working farm near the Murrumbateman wine region.

places.name: Brindabella Hills Winery
places.why: Weekend wine by the glass on the terrace or a set-menu lunch above the Murrumbidgee, 25 minutes from the city.

places.name: Lark Hill Winery
places.why: Biodynamic cool-climate winery at 860 m with a courtyard cellar door and weekend restaurant service.

places.name: Lake George Winery
places.why: Boutique pinot noir and chardonnay with lunch Wednesday to Sunday on a 300-acre vineyard, with tiny-home stays.

places.name: Norton Road Wines
places.why: Family cellar door in Wamboin pouring small-batch pinot noir and riesling, with a BBQ restaurant close by.

places.name: Gallagher Wines
places.why: Family cellar door where winemaker Greg Gallagher often pours his sparkling and riesling, with cheese and preserves on sale.

places.name: Eden Road Wines
places.why: Cool-climate wines tasted at a cellar door 30 minutes from the city, on the Barton Highway side of Murrumbateman.

places.name: Murrumbateman Winery
places.why: One of the region's oldest wineries (1973); riesling and shiraz tastings daily, dog and child friendly.

places.name: Surveyors Hill Vineyards
places.why: Women-run vineyard with a cellar door and bistro open weekends, with accommodation on the property.

places.name: Sapling Yard Cellar Door
places.why: Italian-style wines poured at a reclaimed-timber bar in Bungendore village, with cheese boards from Scrumpers Kitchen next door.

places.name: Gundog Estate Cellar Door
places.why: Dog-friendly tastings in the renovated stables of the Royal Hotel, with lunch from the neighbouring Grazing restaurant.

places.name: Contentious Character Urban Cellar Door
places.why: Canberra District wines tasted in town; the cellar door moved here from the Wamboin vineyard. Indoors.

places.name: Canberra Cellar Door
places.why: Saturday pop-up where six Canberra District wines are poured by the lake, a quick tasting without driving out to Murrumbateman.

places.name: Win's Creek Meadery
places.why: Taste honey mead flights, cider and craft beer in an 1879 inn, with pizza and a honey shop; one of few meaderies around Canberra.

places.name: The Canberra Distillery
places.why: Small-batch gin, whisky and rum made on site, with a cellar door and shop for tastings. Indoors.

places.name: Big River Distilling Co
places.why: Craft gin distillery in the Dairy Road precinct with weekend tours and tastings of three spirits. Indoors.

places.name: Ambrosia Distillery and Lounge
places.why: Flavoured vodka and native-botanical gin from a Dairy Road distillery, with a cocktail lounge next door. Indoors.

places.name: Underground Spirits
places.why: Canberra gin distillery with a cellar door, plus a seasonal Floriade Gin Garden. Indoors.

places.name: Lager House by Capital Brewing Co
places.why: Neighbourhood pub pouring tank-fresh lagers from three tanks, with a wood-fired grill kitchen. Indoors, good for a group.

places.name: Majura Valley Farm
places.why: Farm gate shop with eggs, vegetables, flowers and lamb, and an autumn sunflower maze that families walk through.

places.name: Blackwattle Alpaca Farm
places.why: Book a walk and hand-feeding with alpacas and llamas, then browse the yarn shop and cafe.

places.name: Blue Frog Truffle Farm
places.why: Join a family-run truffle hunt with dogs on Sundays in the mid-June to mid-August season, 5 km from the ACT border.

places.name: The Truffle Farm
places.why: Winter truffle hunt among an oak forest 15 minutes from the city, as a hunt, brunch or degustation.

places.name: Turalla Truffles
places.why: Bungendore truffle growers selling fresh truffles and hosting a degustation lunch in winter.

places.name: Tanbella Orchard
places.why: Pick your own apples, pears and nashi on an autumn day, a short drive from the city; open late January to May only.

places.name: O'Connor Dog Park
places.why: Fenced off-leash dog park in the inner north with separate yards for big and small dogs, agility gear, benches and shade.

places.name: Duffy Dog Park (Weston Creek)
places.why: Fenced dog park with separate large- and small-dog areas, dirt, grass and woodchip to run on, a shade sail and benches.

places.name: Greenway Dog Park (Lake Tuggeranong)
places.why: Dog park beside Lake Tuggeranong with big eucalypts for shade, open grass, benches and two play areas split by dog size.

places.name: Forde Dog Park
places.why: Fenced dog park inside Forde Heritage Park with agility hoops, hurdles and pipes; barbecues, a playground and trails are next door.

places.name: Franklin Dog Park
places.why: New fenced off-leash park with an agility area, grassed space for fetch, a small shelter and dog-waste bag dispensers.

places.name: Lanyon Dog Park
places.why: Fenced off-leash park opened Nov 2025, with separate grass areas for small and large dogs, agility gear, a shelter and a drinking fountain.

places.name: Farrer Nature Play & Adventure Trail
places.why: Nature-based play and adventure trail where kids climb, crawl and explore; one of the ACT Government's favourite play spots in Woden Weston Molonglo.

places.name: Ruth Park Playground
places.why: Playground by Holden's Creek Pond in Coombs with a water pump kids can play with on a warm day.

places.name: Joey Park Playground
places.why: Neighbourhood playground on Bettong Avenue in Throsby, picked in the ACT Government's list of favourite play spots in Gungahlin.

places.name: Ridgeline Park
places.why: Ridge-top playground in Denman Prospect with climbing nets and tunnels, and outdoor fitness equipment in the same park.

places.name: Denman Village Park Splash Pad
places.why: Splash pad opposite the Denman Prospect shops with several fountains of different sizes, handy on a hot day.

places.name: Forde Heritage Park
places.why: Shaded playground with swings, slides and climbing frames, a covered picnic area, toilets and a trail lined with outdoor fitness equipment.

places.name: Wildbark Nature Play Space
places.why: Nature play beside the Mulligans Flat visitor centre with concrete tunnels, a fallen tree to climb and log steppers.

places.name: Callum Brae Nature Reserve
places.why: Quiet woodland reserve known as a birdwatching hotspot for threatened woodland birds, with marked walking tracks; no dogs.

places.name: Farrer Ridge Nature Reserve
places.why: Gentle ridge between the Woden and Tuggeranong valleys, popular for walking, running and cycling; dogs on leash on tracks.

places.name: Gossan Hill Nature Reserve
places.why: Small hill reserve in south-east Belconnen with a 2.5 km loop and unusual rock formations; dogs on leash.

places.name: Gungaderra Grasslands Nature Reserve
places.why: Grassland reserve rising to wooded Gungahlin Hill, dotted with old scribbly gums, with quiet management trails to walk.

places.name: McQuoids Hill Nature Reserve
places.why: Small hill reserve in the west of the Tuggeranong Valley with views of the Murrumbidgee River; the National Trail follows its western edge.

places.name: Nadjung Mada Nature Reserve
places.why: Woodland and grassland reserve in eastern Gungahlin where Superb Parrots feed in breeding season; quiet walking and birdwatching.

places.name: Percival Hill Nature Reserve
places.why: Reserve beside Ginninderra Creek with rare wildflowers and orchids; walk the tracks with a dog on leash.

places.name: Tuggeranong Hill Nature Reserve
places.why: A steep track climbs to the summit for views over the Tuggeranong Valley and the Bullen Range.

places.name: Wanniassa Hills Nature Reserve
places.why: Short ridge walk with sweeping views of southern Canberra, good birdwatching and spring wildflowers.

places.name: Crace Grasslands Nature Reserve
places.why: Grassland reserve that rises to the rocky Crace Hill knoll at 622 m, with grassy tracks for a quiet walk; no dogs.

places.name: Budjan Galindji Grasslands Nature Reserve
places.why: Small grassland and woodland reserve in Franklin where migratory Latham's Snipe visit the seasonal wetlands.

places.name: Justice Robert Hope Park
places.why: Flat low woodland of scattered mature trees on the lower slopes of Mount Majura, an easy bush stroll in the inner north.

places.name: Barrer Hill walks (Molonglo River Reserve)
places.why: Easy 1.8 km Barrer Circuit plus a short summit track on Barrer Hill, with wide views over the Molonglo River Reserve; bikes allowed.

places.name: Mount Rogers Reserve
places.why: Short, easy and popular 2 km loop in the northern suburbs; a quick bush walk close to Belconnen.

places.name: Church Rock Heritage Loop
places.why: A 2.5 km loop of about an hour at Tidbinbilla past the Flints homestead site and Church Rock.

places.name: London Bridge Walk
places.why: A 4.5 km circuit at Googong Foreshores out to a heritage-listed natural rock arch and the London Bridge Homestead site.

places.name: Mount McDonald Summit Track
places.why: Moderate 3.8 or 5.2 km return walk of two to three hours to a summit with views back over Canberra.

places.name: Shepherds Lookout
places.why: Short 1.2 km return walk from Stockdill Drive to a lookout over the Murrumbidgee River; dogs may run off leash here.

places.name: One Tree Hill Walk
places.why: Longer walk of about 8.5 km return from near Hall up One Tree Hill, rewarded with wide views over the north.

places.name: Uriarra Loop
places.why: A 3.5 km walk along sandy Murrumbidgee River banks with views; allow two to two and a half hours.

places.name: Mindjagari Track
places.why: Roughly 26 km network of difficult management trails and walking tracks in Namadgi that can be linked into longer routes.

places.name: Namadgi Visitor Centre Woodland Walk
places.why: Easy 1 km loop through grassy woodland from the Namadgi Visitor Centre, with displays on Gudgenby and an Aboriginal scarred tree.

places.name: Brandy Flat Walk
places.why: A 10 km return walk from Glendale Crossing through box woodland and dry forest to Brandy Flat Hut; the southern half is steep.

places.name: Birrigai Time Trail
places.why: A walk at Tidbinbilla that tells the culture and history of the Ngunnawal people, including a rock shelter.

places.name: Lennox Gardens
places.why: Lakeside gardens with a red gravel boulevard to the water, the Canberra Beijing Garden, free barbecues and outdoor fitness gear.

places.name: Dairy Farmers Hill Lookout
places.why: 360-degree views over Canberra from the top of Dairy Farmers Hill, with the eagle sculpture Nest III and a picnic table.

places.name: Regatta Point Lookout
places.why: Grassy hill overlooking Lake Burley Griffin with toilets and picnic shelters, a handy lakeside spot for a picnic.

places.name: National Rose Gardens
places.why: Spring rose displays, wisteria on pergolas and shady lawns next to Old Parliament House, good for a picnic.

places.name: Woden Town parkrun
places.why: Free weekly timed 5 km run or walk every Saturday at 8 am in Woden Town Park beside Yarralumla Creek, with no road crossings.

places.name: Tuggeranong parkrun
places.why: Free weekly 5 km run or walk on the Lake Tuggeranong foreshore from Tuggeranong Town Park; a fairly flat out-and-back.

places.name: Gungahlin parkrun
places.why: Free weekly 5 km run or walk around the flat loop of Yerrabi Pond, open to joggers, walkers and parkrun regulars.

places.name: Burley Griffin parkrun
places.why: Free weekly 5 km parkrun at Weston Park beside Lake Burley Griffin, open to runners, joggers and walkers.

places.name: Umbagong District parkrun
places.why: Free weekly 5 km parkrun at Umbagong District Park in Latham, starting a short walk from parking at the Kippax shops.

places.name: Wagi Bridge parkrun
places.why: Free weekly 5 km parkrun in Gungahlin, two laps of the shared path around the Wagi Bridge footbridge.

places.name: Athllon Park Disc Golf Course

places.name: Eddison Park Skatepark
places.why: One of the ACT's seven major skateparks, for skateboarders and scooter riders of all levels; lit until 10 pm.

places.name: Yerrabi Skatepark
places.why: Major skatepark beside Yerrabi Pond for skateboarders and scooter riders of all levels; lit until 10 pm.

places.name: Warehouse Circus
places.why: Circus classes from tumbling and acrobalance to aerials, for ages from tiny tots to adults.

places.name: Corin Forest
places.why: Alpine slide down a 1.2 km forest track in summer, snow play and beginner snow slopes in winter, about 45 minutes from the city.

places.name: Majura Valley Farm Sunflower Maze
places.why: Wander the sunflower maze in March on the ACT's oldest working farm, ten minutes from the city; the farm gate shop is open daily.

places.name: Quizzic Alley
places.why: Indoors: Harry Potter-themed shop that runs layered potion-making classes for kids in the school holidays.

places.name: Canberra Archery Club
places.why: Beginner come-and-try archery with coaches and equipment provided at the city's oldest archery club.

places.name: Cycle City Hire (Stromlo Forest Park)
places.why: Hire a full-suspension mountain bike or a toddler balance bike at Stromlo Forest Park on weekends; a shuttle runs up the mountain.

places.name: Gold Creek Country Club
places.why: Public-access 18-hole par 72 golf course designed by Bruce Devlin, with a grassed driving range and hire clubs.

places.name: Woden Gardenland
places.why: Indoors: soft play for ages 1 to 6 with climbing, crawling and sliding among Canberra-themed artwork.

places.name: MarketQuest
places.why: Indoors: slides plus rope and agility platforms for kids, inside Marketplace Gungahlin.

places.name: Ninja Parc
places.why: Indoors: ninja-style obstacle course for ages 6 and up, soft play for under 8s and climbing walls.
